newsitem.title: UK: Britain endorses Annan as new U.N. head.
newsitem.headline: Britain endorses Annan as new U.N. head.

text.p: Britain said on Saturday it endorsed the appointment of Ghana's Kofi Annan as the next secretary-general of the United Nations.
"I have the highest regard for Mr Annan, with whom we have worked very closely for many years," Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said in a statement.
"He has enormous experience of the U.N. in all its aspects including administration and finance as well as the key political issues," he said.
"His experience and outstanding personal qualities make him ideally qualified to lead the U.N. in tackling the many urgent tasks which it currently faces.
"I am sure that he will fill this vitally important post with great distinction. The British government will give him its full support," he said.

Annan, 58, was chosen by the U.N. Security Council on Friday to be the world body's next secretary-general, succeeding Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali whose hopes for a second term were derailed by Washington.

The career diplomat, currently U.N. undersecretary-general for peacekeeping operations, won the support of all 15 Security Council members after France dropped its veto threat. His selection now has to be ratified by the 185-nation General Assembly.
Annan, who is due to take up the appointment on January 1, will become the seventh secretary-general in U.N. history and the first from sub-Sahara Africa.
Swedish Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen said Annan had done a "very good job" in his previous posts.
"I welcome (his appointment)...we know him well," she told reporters at the European Union summit in Dublin.
